title: Where values live, and when they are collected

questions.stem: Where does this page say the value of an `int` field of an object lives?

options.text: On the stack of the thread that created the object
options.says: The page puts only a local variable's primitive on the stack.

options.text: In a separate heap object that the field points to
options.says: A primitive holds its value directly; only a reference points at an object.

options.text: Inside the object itself, which sits on the heap
options.says: The page says a field lives inside its object, and objects are on the heap.

questions.stem: Why does this page say its `GarbageCollectionDemo` prints different output on different runs?

options.text: `System.gc()` is only a request, and the JVM may exit before finalizers run
options.says: That is the page's explanation of why the messages come and go.

options.text: `finalize()` runs on a thread the scheduler picks afresh for every object
options.says: The page names a single finalizer thread that may not get to run at all.

options.text: `obj2` stays reachable until `main` returns, so it is collected much later
options.says: The page says obj2 becomes eligible as soon as createObjects() exits.
